summary.tldr: Bans the export of thermal coal from Canada unless the Environment and Transport ministers issue a permit.
what_it_does: Prohibits exporting thermal coal from Canada unless the exporter has a permit from the Minister of the Environment and the Minister of Transport.
Defines thermal coal as coal used to generate electricity, and certain bituminous, sub-bituminous, lignite and agglomerated lignite, but not metallurgical bituminous coal.
Allows permits only when the ministers believe the export is needed to address an imminent threat to human health, safety or the environment, and lets them set conditions.
Requires the ministers to publish permit decisions, reasons and prescribed documents on a Government of Canada website.
Makes illegal exports, or breaking permit conditions, an offence punishable by fines up to $6 million or $12 million on indictment, and up to $4 million or $8 million on summary conviction.
Brings the law into force on a day set by the Governor in Council, after consulting trade unions whose members are likely to be affected, and no later than one year after royal assent.
summary.background: The bill says thermal coal exports include thermal coal that is imported into Canada or transported in transit through Canada. It does not include metallurgical bituminous coal.
